Subject: POC trial success criteria & next steps

Hey Alex  great speaking with you today. Recap below from our discovery and proposed next steps for the POC/trial. Please confirm that this matches Atlas's expectations.

High-level success criteria (what we should measure):
- Latency: p95 generation latency < 200 ms for production payloads (exclude cold starts); track both server-side and end-to-end where applicable.
- Throughput: sustained 100 requests/sec for the main inference path (concurrent user profile), with spike tolerance to 200 rps for short bursts.
- Cost: modeled cost <= $0.0006 per token (target cost per 1M tokens as a sanity check).
- Quality: automated accuracy for intent classification >= 90% on a holdout of 5k labeled queries; human acceptability >= 85% in a randomized blind review (rubric to be defined).
- Safety/Hallucination: factual error rate < 2% on the evaluation set; critical failures (incorrect payment instructions) must be zero tolerance.

Evaluation plan / instrumentation:
- Atlas to share a 5k-sample anonymized test set (covering high-frequency intents + edge cases).
- Redwood will run baseline using current production prompts and a controlled load generator; we will provide p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, throughput curves, and token-counted cost estimates.
- Marissa will coordinate human review and scoring rubric for the acceptability metric.

Ownership & roles:
- Jordan Blake: POC owner, primary contact for commercial/acceptance.
- Marissa Cole: success metrics & quality evaluation owner.
- Marcus Lin: infra/setup  staging environment, access, and allowlist.

Timeline (proposed):
- Nov 24: Atlas provides test set + IPs for allowlist.
- Nov 27: Kickoff + environment handoff (3045 minutes).
- Dec 4: Baseline results (latency/throughput/cost + initial quality numbers).
- Dec 20: End of trial, final report & go/no-go decision.

Immediate next steps (please reply to confirm):
1) Atlas to share the anonymized test set and preferred measurement rules (e.g., whether to include warm-up).
2) Atlas to confirm staging IPs and SSO/credential approach (we support API key and SSO for staging).
3) Redwood to share POC plan doc and access instructions (Marcus will set up staging).

If that looks good I'll send calendar invites for Nov 27 kickoff and loop in Marcus for the setup.

Thanks  looking forward to getting started.

 Jordan Blake

- For cost: can you provide modeled estimates for 1M and 5M tokens using the baseline config? That will help our finance team.
- Quality rubric: Priya will lead the security/compliance side and will also want to review the human evaluation rubric  Priya, looping you in.

Hi all  attaching the POC setup doc (POC_MA_Plan_v2.pdf) with environment details. Summary: staging cluster will be provisioned in the us-west-2 region and should be ready by Nov 24 EOD once we have the following from Atlas:
- IPs for allowlist (CIDR or specific ranges)
- Preferred auth method (API key or SAML SSO)
- S3 bucket for test dataset or permission to upload into our staging bucket (we can provide presigned URLs)

Notes on measurement: we will run warm-up for 5 minutes and report both warm and steady-state metrics. p95 will be calculated on steady-state requests only unless Atlas requests otherwise. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and tail-latency charts with token counts.

Quick how-to (upload + run):
1) Upload test_set.csv to s3://redwood-poc-atlas/ (we will send presigned URL).
2) Use the staging API key (sent via secure channel) to run the load generator:
   curl -X POST "https://staging-api.redwood.com/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"inputs": [ ... ] }'
